title: OPORP: One Permutation + One Random Projection

problem.claim: The method addresses estimation involving the relationship between two vectors, such as embeddings, with cosine similarity p and common embedding dimensions D = 256–4096.

contributions.claim: OPORP is presented as a count-sketch variant that uses fixed-length binning and normalization for estimation.

The procedure permutes data vectors, applies an i.i.d. random projection by Hadamard multiplication, partitions the D columns into k equal-length bins, aggregates each bin, and normalizes the resulting k samples to unit l2 norm.
The authors give an estimation-variance expression involving s, A, D, k, and p, under A ≥ 0 and s ≥ 1, and state that it reveals key properties of the scheme.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an estimation-variance result for the proposed scheme and state that it reveals several key properties.

narrative_sequence.summary: OPORP is introduced as a count-sketch variant using fixed-length binning and normalization.
The method applies a permutation and random projection, aggregates values into k equal-length bins, and normalizes the resulting samples.
An estimation-variance expression is reported with conditions A ≥ 0 and s ≥ 1.

source_observation.claim: The scheme combines permutation, random projection, equal-length bin aggregation, and unit-l2 normalization.

interpretation.claim: The abstract frames the estimator as a compact multi-step transformation of vector data.

application.claim: This may be relevant to embedding-based applications where dimensions commonly range from 256 to 4096.
